messages:
sophia: heads-up: ran the mixed-precision rollout benchmark this morning — saw a 9% p50 regression on long-context queries when switching to per-channel int8 kernels with our current calibration set :eyes:

kyle: ugh. are we sure it's the calib set and not kernel scheduling or batching heuristics? did you repro with the old kernels?

sophia: yes — swapped kernel back to fp8/bfloat fallback and p50 went back to baseline. same hardware, same batcher. logs attached below. looks correlated with KV cache warmup on conversational tails.

zhang: can you paste the perf snippet? also what was the sample composition for calibration?

sophia: ```
perf summary: model-x (nvfuser-int8-per-channel)
- short (<=128): p50 -3% (better)
- mid (128-1024): p50 -1%
- long (>1024): p50 +9% (worse)
kv-warmup hit-rate dropped ~12% for long tails
calib set size: 15k sequences (mostly web+wiki dialogs, 92% <512 tokens)
calib method: per-channel minmax + percentile clip 99.9
```

anita: that sampling bias is expected — our calib set underrepresents long-tail prefixes so per-channel scale quant becomes unstable on rare outlier channels.

maya: are we using per-tensor fallback for problematic layers? might help but could bloat memory.

luis: we should avoid ad-hoc per-layer fallbacks at runtime. propose two things: 1) short-term rollback to per-tensor int8 for prod; 2) longer-term: introduce "tail-aware" calibration sampling and a two-pass reweighting to preserve outliers.

kyle: +1 for rollback if SLA impact. For the sampling idea, what does two-pass reweighting mean here?

luis: pass1: uniform sample across buckets of sequence length and token frequency to estimate channel activation distributions. pass2: oversample buckets with high variance/outlier channels and compute per-channel calibration with clipped percentiles tuned per-bucket. keeps global sample size manageable.

zhang: sounds reasonable. question: does this change the quantization math or just the stats? i.e., per-channel scale still computed same way but with weighted samples?

anita: exactly. we compute scales with weighted quant stats and optionally use a robust estimator (trimmed mean/std) for channels with heavy tails. avoids a single outlier dominating scale.

perf-bot: perf-regression-detection: alert triggered for model-x on stage at 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z — delta p50 +9% vs baseline, affected traffic 18% :warning:

sophia: proposed action plan: roll back to per-tensor int8 for model-x on stage now, start calibration sweep with tail-aware sampler (15k -> 25k effective with reweighting), and run A/B perf/quality checks for 48h. I'll open a PR with sampler code.

kyle: sgtm. please include a tiny reproducer and a short perf hash so infra can pin kernels during test. also add a KV-cache warmup metric in the dashboard (miss rate by prefix length).

maya: can we also try a small experiment: leave kernels as-is but add a KV prefix cache priming step for long contexts and measure p50 delta? cheap to test.

luis: good idea. cheap ops first. i'll schedule a quick experiment on dedicated infra after rollback.

sophia: thanks all — filing runbook steps now and tagging @kyle @luis for rollout coordination. if no objections i'll trigger rollback in 10m. :thumbsup:
